description: A literal unit default fills omitted quantity calls without replacing a supplied zero
code:
def total(quantity, unit = 5) => quantity * unit
one = total(2)
zero = total(2, 0)
assert(one, 10)
assert(zero, 0)
[one, zero]

description: Typed functions and parenthesized arrows bind signed finite literal defaults
code:
def scale(value: Number, factor: Number = 0.5) => value * factor
adjust = (value, offset = -2) => value + offset
assert(scale(6), 3)
assert(adjust(5), 3)
[scale(6), adjust(5)]

description: Constructor and method defaults create independent effective values for each instance
code:
class Counter(seed = 1):
    this.count = seed
    def advance(delta = 2):
        this.count += delta
        return this.count
first = Counter()
second = Counter()
one = first.advance().value
two = second.advance(4).value
assert(first.count, 3)
assert(second.count, 5)
assert(one, 3)
assert(two, 5)
[one, two]

description: Defaulted parameter version zero is the effective literal in each fresh invocation frame
code:
step = 100
def sample(step = 4) => [step = step + 1, step@first, step@last]
one = sample()
two = sample(9)
assert(one, [5, 4, 5])
assert(two, [10, 9, 10])
assert(step, 100)
[one, two]
